payload.text: Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to suppress electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism. An independent audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee, retracting the earlier higher claim. The cell delivers 148 Wh/kg, with a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Its operating limit is a 4 °C floor, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.
